newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close on a rally following rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close on a rally following rate cut.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed much stronger on Wednesday, with spreads to U.S. bonds narrowing, following a Bank of Canada rate cut which took much of the market by surprise, analysts said.

"It was enough to give the market a very firm bid," said David Adamo, managing director of fixed-income research with Scotia Capital Markets. "We've got a market that's got quite a head of steam on it."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$1.05 at C$105.05 to yield 7.556 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark which gained 15/32 to yield 6.84 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 72 basis points from 76 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The Bank of Canada this morning cut short-term interest rates for the eighth time this year, lowering its key Bank Rate by 25 basis points to 4.0 percent.
It was the seventh time this year the bank has cut rates independent of an easing in U.S. rates. The central bank has now lowered short-term rates by 200 basis points this year.
"Now was probably the best time they could go because the currency had some strength and the overall market tone was good," said Adamo.

Dealers said debate remains in the market about whether today's ease marks the end of the easing cycle. Analysts said there is some speculation the bank will cut rates further if the currency appreciates sharply, effective tightening monetary conditions.
In new issue news, the Government of Canada today auctioned C$2.8 billion of 5.5 percent bonds due February 1, 2000. The issue had an average yield of 5.572 percent with a price of 99.777.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.69 to C$100.19 to yield 6.972 percent.
The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 11/32 to yield 6.59 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds narrowed to 38 basis points from 43 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.50 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.03 percent.
